messages:
alex: Heads up — after the CUDA 13.1 driver rollout to canaries we see a ~25% p50 token throughput regression on A100 for long-context workloads (8k+). CI perf alert fired.

prateek: oof. can you paste the perf numbers and which kernel variants got selected? :thinking_face:

alex: yes. quick numbers from canary qps test (batching=dynamic, kv cache warm):
```
old-driver (12.x): p50 = 18.2 tok/s, p95 = 10.4 tok/s
new-driver (13.1): p50 = 13.6 tok/s, p95 = 7.8 tok/s
```

alex: autotuner logs show a sweep and it picked the cuda-gemm-gelupack-v1 kernel for seq>=2048; previously it picked cuda-gemm-arch-asm-v2 on the same machines.

maya: do we have profiler traces? nvprof/nvtx spans would help see whether it's membound or compute-bound now.

alex: attached quick nvprof stack from canary:
```
GPU api time breakdown:
copy H2D: 3.1%
kernel: 92.4%
  gemm_kernel (cuda-gemm-gelupack-v1): 68%
  aten_op (other): 24%
warp efficiency dropped by ~12% vs 12.x
```

sara: interesting — warp efficiency + choice of gelu pack kernel. I remember driver 13 had a scheduler change that performs worse on some fused kernels.

prateek: could be ABI or PTX codegen differences making our asm kernels worse, so autotuner fell back to a different kernel that happens to be slower on A100 micro-ops.

maya: two quick checks: 1) force the old kernel pick in config for a single canary node group; 2) run a microbench of both kernels with representative seq lengths and batch shapes.

alex: tried forcing kernel override via runtime config on one canary pool: set KERNEL_PREFERENCE=["cuda-gemm-arch-asm-v2","cuda-gemm-gelupack-v1"] — p50 recovered to 17.9 tok/s (approx previous). Good signal.

ops: rollback plan options: (A) rollback driver 13.1 on canaries to 12.x, (B) pin kernel preference in runtime until we get proper autotuner patch, (C) force model variant with shorter fused ops. Pros/cons?

prateek: (B) is lowest-risk and fastest. We should still prepare (A) for if we see other regressions (smoothing, stability). Also we need a fix in autotuner: add driver-version-aware kernel scoring or a post-upgrade re-evaluation window.

sara: scheduler: should we modify batching heuristics? long-seq requests trigger a different codepath; maybe batching is increasing variance and exposing the bad kernel more. If we limit batch size for seq>2048 we could reduce p95 tail.

maya: agree. I'll run microbench controlling batch size and KV cache warm/cold to see impact. Note: KV cache behavior interacts — when cache hits are high, compute dominates; when cache misses on long-context, memory copy patterns change and can hit the slower kernel more.

ci-bot: PERF ALERT: regressed p50 by 25% on eng-runtime/canary. See run: https://ci.internal/perf/1795 :rotating_light:

alex: immediate actions taken: pinned kernel pref on canary pool, increased perf sampling to 1/min, notified SRE. Next: ramp pin to 10% of prod for 2h then full rollback if stable.

ops: command to pin kernel in runtime (canary pool):
```
redwoodctl runtime update-pool canary-1 --set kernel_preference='["cuda-gemm-arch-asm-v2"]'
```

prateek: longer term: autotuner change idea: include (driver_version, sm_arch) in the scoring key and keep historical perf samples per kernel variant per driver. Also add a fallback grace period: if post-upgrade autotuner picks new kernels, run short A/B microbench before global rollout.

sara: +1. also add a quick health-check job after infra upgrades that runs seq=512, 2048, 8192 microbench and validates against baseline thresholds.

maya: I'll collect the microbench results and post them here. early note: kernel override recovered p50 but p95 still slightly worse — so batching/p95 interaction might need heuristics.

alex: thanks. action items:
- maya: microbench for three seq lengths, batch shapes, kv warm/cold (due EOD).
- prateek: implement a temporary driver-aware scoring flag in autotuner (PR WIP).
- ops: hold driver 13.1 rollout until we confirm autotuner changes or driver vendor patch.

ops: will schedule driver rollback playbook if we see regressions on 10% ramp. tagging infra team.

prateek: I'll open a ticket with vendor (NVIDIA) with the kernel perf traces and PTX diffs. Might be a codegen issue.

alex: any objections to keeping this pin in place for 48h? We need time to validate.

sara: no objections. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: NOTE: perf sampling enabled and alert sensitivity increased for canary cluster.
